text:
marie: FYI starting schema migration for tenant_profiles tonight 02:00 UTC. Using deploybot with ratecap=120/s across backfill workers. Tagging @oncall-db @sam @leo

 deploybot: Scheduled migration run created by marie. Command:
```
/deploybot run migration tenant_profiles --ratecap 120 --workers 8 --holdpoint canary:10%
```

 sam: Quick Q — if two migrations hit DB at same time, how does ratecap tiebreak work? We had a queue pileup last month.

 leo: Good point. current behavior: per-worker token bucket + global limiter per schema. If global saturates, deploybot queues by start_ts. That caused fairness issues.

 sam: I'd rather prefer lease-based tiebreak: coordinator tries to acquire migration lease (key in redis), if fail -> backoff jitter + exponential. Should also expose manual takeover.

 marie: Agree. For tonight we can't change coordinator. Plan B: manual tiebreak — ops will pin one migration to priority and pause the other. I'll add holdpoint flags.

 oncall-db: Prep checklist: a) preflight verify pg_stat_activity for long transactions, b) set statement_timeout=5m for migration workers, c) watch pg_locks and lock_waits metric. If lock wait > 30s for >5 hosts -> pause.

 marie: Rollback plan in thread: 1) /deploybot pause migration tenant_profiles
2) run reverse SQL: `psql -f migrations/2026-02-12-reverse-tenant-profiles.sql`
3) unpin feature flag if enabled
4) escalate to DBA if locks persist

 deploybot: Canary progress: 10% -> 25% complete, no schema-lock errors. Logs: `backfill: processed 48k rows, rate 118r/s`

 leo: If we need manual takeover, do: `/deploybot set-priority migration tenant_profiles --priority high` then pause other job. I'll standby.

 sam: I'll be on-call 01:30-03:30 UTC. If we hit DB saturation, I'll trigger hard abort and run reverse script. :thumbsup:

 marie: Thanks — I'll post a short release note in #release-notes when canary hits 50%.
